body:
Big multiplication problems are just small ones put together.

To find 6 × 43, break 43 into tens and ones:
6 × 40 = 240
6 × 3 = 18
240 + 18 = 258

An area model shows each part as a rectangle, and the parts are called partial products.

Division works in parts too. To share 96 among 4, share 80, then share 16: 20 + 4 = 24.

Sometimes there is a remainder, and you have to think about what it means. If 75 students ride in vans that hold 8, you need 10 vans, not 9, so nobody is left behind!
title: Big Numbers, Smart Strategies
